subject: Clarifying SIG item: 'Data Flow & Processor Responsibilities' — Apex Security
messages:
From: Layla Torres <layla.torres@apexbiotech.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Apex Security Team <security@apexbiotech.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SIG Q12 clarification: 'processor responsibilities'

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the SIG draft — we reviewed the responses and have a couple of follow-ups. Q12 seems to ask for both (a) whether Redwood acts as a processor for customer data and (b) the downstream processor responsibilities. The language in the SIG isn't explicit about whether you're expecting an operational list (who does what) or legal contract text.

Can you confirm:
- Do you intend us to provide the list of technical subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, monitoring vendors) and their roles, or a short statement that Redwood acts as a processor and customers retain control?
- If you want the technical list, do you accept a reference to our vendor inventory link and redacted service descriptions, or do you need full contact-level details?

We can jump on a 30-minute call to walk through. We're aiming to complete the SIG by EOD Friday if possible.

Thanks,
Layla
Layla Torres
Senior InfoSec Manager
Apex Biotech

--
Attachment: apex-question-highlights.pdf (stapled excerpt of SIG items for review)

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Layla Torres <layla.torres@apexbiotech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG Q12 clarification: 'processor responsibilities'

Hi Layla — thanks for the clear notes and the PDF. Quick answers up front:
- We consider Redwood an independent processor under our standard DPA; customers are controllers.
- For the SIG, we can provide a concise operational list of downstream processors (cloud infra, observability, payment processor) with the role and country of processing.

On the level of detail: a link to our vendor inventory plus a short row-per-vendor (name, role, hosting country, minimal contact) should work for most customers. We avoid sharing contract-level details or indemnities in the SIG — those live in the DPA.

I've asked Marissa (security ops) to attach our draft spreadsheet with proposed responses and to call out anything that might be sensitive. Neha, can you confirm whether the payment processor entry needs redaction for customer PII handling?

If that level works for you, let's do a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 10:00 PT to confirm the final wording. I've tentatively sent a calendar invite.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: SIG Q12 clarification: 'processor responsibilities' — draft responses attached

Hi Layla,

Attached is our proposed response workbook (redwood_sig_responses_v1.xlsx). Sheet 1 has a short textual answer for Q12; Sheet 2 is the vendor table with the fields you requested: vendor name, role (processing/monitoring/backups), primary country, and an anonymized contact email (security@vendor.example).

Quick highlights / rationale:
- We state: "Redwood acts as a processor for customer-submitted content; customers remain controllers and retain rights to data. Downstream processors used by Redwood are listed below with role and country. Contractual obligations are governed by the DPA."
- Vendors that process customer content (e.g., S3 buckets, cache providers) are listed explicitly. Monitoring and analytics vendors are included but marked as "limited-access" where we only share aggregated telemetry.
- Payment processor (Stripe) entry excludes transaction-level PII by design — Neha confirms this is standard.

Action items before our call:
1) Layla: confirm whether anonymized contact emails are ok, or if you need vendor legal contacts.
2) Neha: confirm Stripe cell wording.
3) Jonas: if Apex needs a statement that Redwood will flow down DPA obligations to subprocessors, we can add a short sentence.

Attachments: redwood_sig_responses_v1.xlsx (worked example), apex-question-highlights.pdf (from your earlier mail).

Thanks — happy to discuss on the call.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
